关键词: Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association
主要内容: The Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee (TBAC) of the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association convened on August 1st, 2017, in a closed session at the Hay Adams Hotel. All members, except Michelle Neal, were present. Counselor to the Secretary Craig Phillips, Fiscal Assistant Secretary David Lebryk, Acting Assistant Secretary for Financial Markets Monique Rollins, Director of the Office of Debt Management Fred Pietrangeli, and Deputy Director of the Office of Debt Management John Dolan welcomed the Committee. Other Treasury staff members present included Dave Chung, Ken Phelan, Jared Roscoe, Rozlyn Engel, Tom Katzenbach, Chris Cameron, Mike Puglia, Renee Tang, Brandon Taylor, and Elisha Whipkey. Federal Reserve Bank of New York staff members Lorie Logan, Nathaniel Wuerffel, and Nick Steele were also present. Director Pietrangeli discussed key takeaways, including a forecast of $501 billion in net marketable borrowing for FY 2018 Q1, assuming the debt limit will be increased. He also noted the Federal Reserve’s clarity on balance sheet normalization and its implications for Treasury borrowing needs. The Committee then considered various issuance scenarios to fund SOMA redemptions, with members discussing tradeoffs in different strategies, including costs, flexibility, and the impact on weighted average maturity (WAM). The Committee adjourned at 12:30 p.m. for lunch and reconvened at 1:30 p.m. to continue the discussion. The TBAC meeting on August 1, 2017, discussed the timing of Treasury's strategy decision, suggesting it should be made as early as the November refunding but no later than the first calendar quarter of 2018. The discussion on potential issuance choices and the potential for sizable bill issuance prompted a discussion on the weighted average maturity (WAM). The Committee generally agreed that WAM should remain about the same or increase moving forward. Some members referenced a presentation from the May 2017 TBAC meeting, which suggested that the marginal benefits of extending WAM past the intermediate sector were very low. Other members cautioned about using WAM as a metric for cost and risk. The Committee agreed to discuss the topic of WAM, issuance models, and additional portfolio metrics at some future point. A Committee member also presented findings from a model on the potential effects of balance sheet normalization on other risk assets. The Committee adjourned at 2:45 p.m.
